dedupe_keys.name: cyclingmax world bank cost and benefit analysis tool for cycling facilities

description: CyclingMAX is a web-based cost and benefit scoping tool that World Bank Group staff built to help client countries and decision makers appraise investments in cycling facilities. Its technical background paper, the Cost and Benefit Analysis Tool for Cycling Facilities (October 2024), was written by Feng Guo and Jianhe Du of Progress Analytics LLC with World Bank staff. Coverage: newly built cycling facilities that give cyclists an exclusive bikeway at project level, designed for developing countries where transport data may be very limited. The tool monetises four benefit categories, safety, health (mortality), travel time and the environment, into an annual cash flow, sets them against construction and maintenance costs, and reports the net present value and internal rate of return. Format and access: an online tool with input and result pages, whose results download as a Microsoft Excel file, plus the background paper. Licence and cost: free to use; the paper may be reproduced for noncommercial purposes with full attribution, and the tool is supplied as is without warranty. Caveats: results rest on default factors and the user's own inputs; the World Bank does not vouch for their accuracy in a given setting. It can be used to attach monetised benefits to cycling demand from network flow models when comparing investment scenarios. It relates to the WHO HEAT tool and the Copenhagen cycle superhighway appraisal in the catalogue.
